technical_issues.issue: Claims Rachel will not ship if any possibility of physical harm but will ship higher-likelihood data-loss failure because competitor would – misrepresents ethical baseline.
Cites EA Code clauses 2.1b, 2.3b, 3.3 with garbled symbols and paraphrasing; no quantitative risk/reliability analysis for defect likelihood.

overall: Well-structured report presenting balanced for/against arguments supported by EA Code and relevant case studies, concluding clearly for Not to Ship with actionable recommendations. Lacks quantitative evidence, visual elements, and deeper stakeholder differentiated decision analysis.

feedback.summary: You produced a well-structured, balanced report with a clear Not to Ship conclusion supported by EA Code and case studies. Your introduction and stakeholder analysis were strong. To reach Excellent overall, add quantitative risk analysis, visual elements, and stakeholder-differentiated recommendations with polished referencing.
next_steps: Add a simple quantitative risk/reliability estimate for the defect in The Most Ethical Path and reference it to move C4 to Excellent.
Add a visual element - e.g., stakeholder impact matrix or risk matrix - in your Discussion and fix the DICUSSION heading typo to lift C5.
Expand your Recommendation with separate decision guidance for government health department, patients, and supplier beyond Rachel/company to reach Excellent in C2 and C3.

criteria.C1: Excellent work. You identified several ethical issues — public safety, integrity, reputation, business survival — and linked them to engineering design and organisational context from INTRODUCTION. Well done listing multi-stakeholder interests. Check stakeholder accuracy: scenario contract is with government health department, not chip contractor.
criteria.C2: You built objective for/against arguments in DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship and The Most Ethical Path. To reach Excellent, add decision-making recommendations differentiated for each stakeholder — e.g., what should government, patients, and supplier expect/do — not just Rachel/company.
criteria.C3: Your abstract-introduction-body-conclusion-recommendation structure makes your argument compelling, and your CONCLUSION justifies Not to Ship well. For Excellent, show systematic ethical impacts for all stakeholders in The Most Ethical Path, linking each back to your conclusion.
criteria.C4: Good use of EA Code and cases like NHS HSSIB and Volkswagen in The Most Ethical Path. For Very Good/Excellent, add quantitative evidence of failure likelihood/impact, remove low-relevance sources like [Apple psychology], and include a figure/table to support risk claims.
criteria.C5: You have all required sections and fluent writing. For Very Good, fix the DICUSSION heading typo you have and URL/formatting issues in References, and add at least one visual element such as a stakeholder map or risk table to support discussion.
